misconception_description: Student believes that the arithmetic operation + has higher precedence than the arithmetic operation /.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekBilanganPrima
kamus
  n, i : integer
  prima : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  if n < 2 then
    prima <- false
  else
    prima <- true
    for i <- 2 to n + 1 / 2 do
      if n mod i == 0 then
        prima <- false
      endif
    endfor
  endif
  output(prima)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student modified the range limit from `num//2` to `num + 1 // 2`. The student believes that addition has higher precedence than division, so they think this expression evaluates as `(num + 1) // 2`, which would check divisors up to roughly half of (num+1). However, due to actual operator precedence, this evaluates as `num + (1 // 2)` = `num + 0` = `num`, which changes the loop to check divisors up to num-1 instead of num//2-1. This makes the algorithm less efficient and potentially changes its behavior for edge cases, though the student believes they're just slightly adjusting the upper bound for thoroughness.
